intro: Each city and town runs its own elections through its local election office (a city or town clerk, or an election commission). The Secretary of the Commonwealth oversees elections statewide.

elections.name: State election
elections.what: Federal, state, and county offices, plus statewide ballot questions. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Every city and town has at least one early voting site, with some hours on both weekends. If your town has more than one site, you can use any of them. Hours are set locally, and many places have short or no hours on Fridays. Schedules are posted at VoteInMA.com by Oct. 10.

src.label: Secretary of the Commonwealth, 2026 Information for Voters, p. 4

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: Register online until 11:59 pm, by mail with a form postmarked by Oct. 24, or in person at your local election office by 5 pm. Online sign-up needs a Massachusetts driver's license or ID.

src.label: Secretary of the Commonwealth, 2026 Information for Voters, p. 4

dates.label: Mail ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Anyone can vote by mail. No reason is needed. Your Vote by Mail application must reach your local election office by 5 pm. The state suggests applying by Oct. 13 if you mail it, or by Oct. 20 if you apply online.

src.label: Secretary of the Commonwealth, 2026 Information for Voters, p. 4

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls open 7 am to 8 pm at your assigned polling place. If you are in line by 8 pm, you can vote. Mail ballots handed in or put in a drop box must arrive by 8 pm. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Nov. 3.

src.label: Secretary of the Commonwealth, 2026 Information for Voters, p. 4
Cambridge Election Commission, 2026 State Election guide (return deadlines)

dates.label: Last day for mailed ballots to arrive
dates.detail: A ballot mailed in the U.S. and postmarked by Election Day counts if it arrives by 5 pm on Nov. 6. If you have not mailed your ballot a week before Election Day, the state suggests using a drop box or handing it in.

src.label: Cambridge Election Commission, 2026 State Election guide

id_rule.text: Most voters do not have to show ID. A poll worker may ask some voters, such as some first-time voters who registered by mail. A photo ID works, or a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document with your name and address. If you are asked and have no ID, you can still vote, but your ballot may be challenged or cast as a provisional ballot.
